The respondent, Mohammad Sanaullah, was first appointed as an ordinary employee in the Nishat Jute Mills Ltd. in 1962 and he was promoted to the post of Assistant Production Officer on 1 July 1982. While he was serving as such in this Mill the Corporation, by an order dated 30 May 1983 transferred him to Karim Jute Mills purportedly under the provisions of Article 17(1) of P.O. 27 of 1972. Respondent took objection to this order of transfer and filed the suit challenging the Corporation's authority to transfer him taking the ground that though the Nishat Jute Mills was a nationalized enterprise placed under the Corporation, yet the enterprise retained its separate entity and independent character as a company incorporated under the Companies Act, that employees of the company are not employees of the Corporation and as such the Corporation got no authority to tarsier him to any other Jute Mills or even to the Corporation itself. The trial Court rejected his contention and dismissed the suit; but the appellate court, namely the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka, accepted his contention, allowed the appeal and on reversing the trial Court's decision decreed the suit holding that the order of transfer was invalid as the Corporation got no jurisdiction, power or authority to make such an order of transfer. This decision has been upheld by the learned Single Judge in revision as stated above. 

 10. For the reasons given above we find that the High Court Division's view of law is erroneous and the decision faulty. Corporation has got power to make the transfer of the respondent. In the result, the appeal is allowed. The impugned judgment and decree of the High Court Division is set aside and that of the trial Court dismissing the suit is restored. In view of the important question of law raised in this case we make no order as to costs.
